name: Venice
matter: A famous island city in North Eastern Italy built across more than 100 small islands in a lagoon.
The city is renowned for its iconic flat-bottomed gondolas and centuries-old Venetian Gothic and Byzantine architecture.
It is also globally famous for its vibrant artistic traditions, particularly Carnival celebrations and delicate hand-blown Murano glass.

name: Florence
matter: Florence is universally celebrated as the birthplace of the Italian Renaissance.
Its historic center is dominated by Brunelleschi’s massive terracotta dome atop the Florence Cathedral (the Duomo)
The city houses world-famous artistic masterpieces, including Michelangelo’s David and Botticelli’s The Birth of Venus.

name: Rome
matter: Rome spans nearly three millennia of history, earning its title as the Eternal City and the cradle of Western civilization.
Ancient monuments like the Colosseum and the Roman Forum stand seamlessly integrated alongside bustling modern streets.
It encloses Vatican City, the world's smallest independent state and the global heart of the Catholic Church.

name: Milan
matter: Home to luxury brands like Armani, Prada and Versace who host world famous events like Milan fashion week
As Italy's financial and business centre Milan is also famous for its fierce football rivalry between AC Milan and Inter Milan
Leonardo Da Vinci's famous 15th century mural The last supper is housed in the city's Convent of Santa Maria Delle Grazie

name: Naples
matter: Naples is one of Europe's oldest continuously inhabited urban centers, steeped in Greek-Roman heritage and vibrant street life.
Universally recognized as the birthplace of traditional wood-fired pizza and rich espresso culture.
Set against the dramatic backdrop of Mount Vesuvius and the ancient ruins of Pompeii and Herculaneum.

name: Amalfi Coast
matter: A dramatic coastline in southern Italy famed for its pastel-colored villages clinging to sheer sea cliffs.
Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site known for fragrant lemon groves, hidden coves, and scenic coastal highways.
Iconic towns like Positano, Amalfi, and Ravello have enchanted artists, writers, and travelers for generations.

name: Bologna
matter: Known as Italy's gastronomic capital, famed worldwide for fresh handmade egg pasta, mortadella, and authentic ragù.
Home to the University of Bologna, established in 1088 and celebrated as the oldest continuously operating university in the world.
Characterized by medieval towers and over 40 kilometers of elegant terracotta porticoes lining the city center.

name: Palermo
matter: The historic capital of Sicily, showcasing a fascinating confluence of Arab, Byzantine, Norman, and Baroque architecture.
Famous for its bustling, vibrant street markets like Ballarò, Vucciria, and Il Capo offering celebrated Sicilian street food.
Home to architectural masterpieces including the Palatine Chapel, the grand Palermo Cathedral, and Teatro Massimo.
